subtype: Approach: groupthink on a weak idea [Pitfall]
passage: In the school workshop in Da Nang, Tuan laid a sketch on the table: a bridge of wooden sticks with one tall arch and no side supports. "This will hold the most weight," he said, and everyone nodded. Nadia frowned at the arch, which looked thin at the base, but said nothing. Linh glanced at Nadia and bit her lip. On test day the arch bowed and cracked under the second weight. The team stared at the pile of sticks. "I thought it might," Nadia said at last. "So did I," said Linh. Tuan looked from one to the other. "Then why did nobody say so?" No one answered. Each of them had thought someone else would speak first.

qa.q: Where was the bridge test held and what happened to the arch?
qa.a: The arch bowed and cracked under the second weight on test day.

qa.q: Why did Nadia stay silent when the plan was shown?
qa.a: Nadia felt doubtful but hesitant to object, probably not wanting to be the only one to disagree with a confident plan.

qa.q: What could the team do differently next time, and why?
qa.a: They could ask each member for a concern before choosing a design, because that lets doubts be voiced without anyone standing alone.

qa.q: How might Tuan feel when learning that two people had doubts?
qa.a: Tuan probably feels surprised and a little hurt, since a concern could have saved the bridge.

grounding: Everyone agrees with the confident member's plan even though two have doubts, the design fails at testing, and the team later admits nobody wanted to be the one to object.
